findings.title: Governed workspaces allow policy bypass via enforce_policy:false on ActionRun creation
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/action-runs with enforce_policy:false, role:viewer (or any role), and a valid action_type_id/target_object_id pair
findings.attack_path: createActionRun checks isWorkspaceGoverned and authorize only when input.enforce_policy !== false. Attacker POSTs action-runs with enforce_policy:false to skip PermissionCheck and policy_denied even when active deny-all policies exist.
findings.impact: Complete bypass of workspace RBAC on the action path: arbitrary governed mutations without policy evaluation or denial audit semantics.
findings.evidence: Static analysis plus local PoC on e79f9aa: workspace with deny-all active policy still accepted createActionRun when enforce_policy:false; action_run completed and object mutated.
findings.remediation: Remove enforce_policy from external request bodies; always enforce policy in governed workspaces or require authenticated platform authority to set an internal bypass flag.

findings.title: ActionRun creation accepts spoofed role without membership or delegation binding
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/action-runs with role:owner (or admin/editor) and principal_id/agent fields chosen by the caller
findings.attack_path: createActionRun passes input.role directly into authorize without verifying the caller holds that workspace membership role or an active AgentDelegation. Attacker claims owner to satisfy allow rules.
findings.impact: Role spoofing defeats policy rules keyed on workspace roles; viewer-equivalent callers can present owner/admin roles and run denied actions.
findings.evidence: authorize(workspaceId, { role: input.role, ... }) uses unauthenticated body fields; no membership lookup on HTTP action-runs route in apps/api/src/server.js.
findings.remediation: Derive role only from verified identity or delegation bearer; reject client-supplied role on unauthenticated routes.

findings.title: Unauthenticated callers can mint AgentDelegation tokens with arbitrary scopes and tools
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: POST /agents to create an agent, then POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/agent-delegations with scopes:[atlas.read,atlas.act,github.pr:create,slack.read], role:owner, allowed_tools:[*]
findings.attack_path: server.js exposes POST /workspaces/:id/agent-delegations without authentication. createAgentDelegation accepts caller-chosen role, scopes, allowed_tools, ttl, and optional goal_contract_id, returning a bearer id usable at POST /agent/tools/:tool.
findings.impact: Self-issued least-privilege bypass: any network client can obtain full agent gateway authority including external integration scopes.
findings.evidence: No auth gate on agent-delegations POST; createAgentDelegation in ontology-store.js records agent.delegation_issued audit with actor=agent_id, not a human principal.
findings.remediation: Require authenticated human/platform authority to issue delegations; agents cannot self-mint per SECURITY_MODEL and zero-trust orchestration skills.

findings.title: Object PATCH mutations skip workspace policy enforcement
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: PATCH /workspaces/{workspace_id}/objects/{object_id} with properties_json altering governed fields (e.g. status, priority, sensitive metadata)
findings.attack_path: updateObjectInstance merges properties and appends object_instance.updated audit events without calling authorize or evaluatePolicy. PATCH route in server.js only applies guardPersonalObjectPatch for personal task status=done, not general policy.
findings.impact: Direct property mutation bypasses deny-by-default policy on the action path for any object field writable via PATCH.
findings.evidence: updateObjectInstance has no isWorkspaceGoverned branch; contrast with createActionRun policy gate at line ~1539.
findings.remediation: Route governed mutations through policy-checked actions or enforce policy on PATCH with explicit action/resource_type mapping.

findings.title: Unauthenticated callers can register custom ActionTypes with arbitrary property effects
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/action-types with effect_json.set_properties_json and copy_input_fields targeting governed object types
findings.attack_path: createActionType is exposed via unauthenticated POST. Attacker defines update_object_properties effects then invokes them through action-runs (with role spoofing or enforce_policy:false).
findings.impact: Attacker-defined action surface enables tailored mutations that policy authors did not anticipate, including exfiltration-shaped property copies.
findings.evidence: server.js action-types POST has no auth; createActionType only validates schema shape, not caller authority.
findings.remediation: Restrict action type creation to authenticated administrators; freeze action catalogs in governed workspaces.

findings.title: Unauthenticated callers can revoke active AgentDelegations (board pause without board)
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: PATCH /workspaces/{workspace_id}/agent-delegations/{delegation_id} with status:revoked
findings.attack_path: Delegation PATCH route accepts status=revoked from any client. revokeAgentDelegation updates status and logs agent.delegation_revoked with actor defaulting to human_authority without verifying a human principal.
findings.impact: Denial-of-service against legitimate agent sessions; false audit attribution implying human authority revoked the delegation.
findings.evidence: PATCH agent-delegations handler only validates status===revoked; no authentication or delegation ownership check before revokeAgentDelegation.
findings.remediation: Require authenticated human/platform authority for revocation; do not accept unauthenticated PATCH on delegations.

findings.title: Unauthenticated callers can inject permissive active policies into any workspace
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/policies with status:active and rules_json allow run_action for viewer on all resource types
findings.attack_path: createPolicy via unauthenticated POST activates allow rules. Once any active policy exists, isWorkspaceGoverned becomes true but attacker-supplied allow rules grant the spoofed roles used on action-runs.
findings.impact: Workspace governance collapse: attacker grants themselves broad allow rules, negating intended deny-by-default posture.
findings.evidence: server.js policies POST without auth; isWorkspaceGoverned checks any active policy, evaluatePolicy honors attacker-controlled rules_json.
findings.remediation: Policy mutations must require authenticated owner/admin authority; consider immutable bootstrap policies for governed workspaces.

findings.title: Unauthenticated callers can inject deny-all policies to deny legitimate workspace actions
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/policies with status:active and deny run_action rules matching all roles and resource types
findings.attack_path: Attacker activates a deny-all policy in a target workspace. Subsequent legitimate action-runs receive 403 policy_denied even when operators expect an open workspace.
findings.impact: Governance denial-of-service: workspace appears governed and rejects all actions until policies are manually cleaned from in-memory store.
findings.evidence: createPolicy accepts arbitrary rules_json; no rate limit or authority check on policy POST.
findings.remediation: Restrict policy creation to trusted principals; separate operator policy templates from tenant-writable configuration.

findings.title: Direct POST /action-runs bypasses agent gateway GoalContract and tool allowlist checks
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/action-runs for action types blocked under an active GoalContract bound to the only legitimate delegation
findings.attack_path: authorizeAgentTool enforces GoalContract allowed/blocked actions for gateway tools, but HTTP action-runs calls createActionRun directly without GoalContract evaluation.
findings.impact: GoalContract constraints are bypassed for mutations reachable via ActionType effects even when agent delegations are properly scoped.
findings.evidence: run_action tool calls createActionRun with delegation role; HTTP action-runs skips authorizeAgentTool GoalContract branch entirely.
findings.remediation: Disallow unauthenticated action-runs in governed workspaces or require delegation bearer that reuses authorizeAgentTool checks.

findings.title: Unauthenticated callers can create permissive GoalContracts and bind them to minted delegations
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/goal-contracts with allowed_actions:[*] and blocked_actions:[] then reference goal_contract_id when minting a delegation
findings.attack_path: goal-contracts POST has no authentication. Attacker creates a contract allowing all tools, mints a delegation with that contract id, and satisfies authorizeAgentTool goal_contract_action_not_allowed checks trivially.
findings.impact: GoalContract layer becomes attacker-controlled, defeating Paperclip/MoO alignment and blocked action lists for agent sessions.
findings.evidence: createGoalContract stores caller-supplied allowed_actions; createAgentDelegation only verifies contract exists and is active, not creator authority.
findings.remediation: GoalContract creation must require authenticated platform authority; delegations cannot bind attacker-created contracts.

findings.title: GoalContract blocked_actions ignored when attacker mints delegation without a contract
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: Mint delegation without goal_contract_id while operator relies on workspace GoalContracts to block tools like github.open_pr
findings.attack_path: authorizeAgentTool only evaluates GoalContract when delegation.goal_contract_id is set. Self-minted delegations omit the contract, skipping blocked_actions enforcement entirely.
findings.impact: Operator assumption that GoalContracts protect a workspace fails when attackers mint unbound delegations with equivalent scopes.
findings.evidence: authorizeAgentTool goal contract branch gated on delegation.goal_contract_id; unauthenticated delegation mint allows omitting the field.
findings.remediation: Require goal_contract_id on all delegations in governed workspaces or enforce workspace-level default contracts on the write path.

findings.title: Reserved workspace IDs can be squatted via unauthenticated POST /workspaces
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: POST /workspaces with id:workspace_personal (or other reserved ids) before legitimate bootstrap
findings.attack_path: createWorkspace accepts caller-supplied id. Attacker registers workspace_personal or workspace_operational_dogfood first; later bootstrapPersonalAtlas or operational scripts hit workspace_conflict or operate on attacker-owned workspace records.
findings.impact: Personal Atlas bootstrap failure or operational dogfood hijack; agents may read/write attacker-controlled workspace metadata.
findings.evidence: createWorkspace uses input.id when provided; server.js POST /workspaces unauthenticated.
findings.remediation: Reserve system workspace ids server-side; reject external id assignment or require platform authority for fixed ids.

findings.title: Personal task blocker graph can be manipulated via unauthenticated link instance creation
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: POST /workspaces/workspace_personal/links with link_type_task_blocks_task connecting attacker tasks to block legitimate personal tasks (or POST after bootstrap squat)
findings.attack_path: createLinkInstance is unauthenticated. Attacker adds blocking edges so assertPersonalTaskCanComplete returns task_blocked for operator tasks, or removes pressure by completing blockers via PATCH/policy bypass paths.
findings.impact: Integrity failure of Personal Atlas dependency graph; next-action selector and task completion gating become attacker-influenced.
findings.evidence: getTaskBlockers trusts link instances from store; links POST in server.js has no auth; LINK_TYPE_TASK_BLOCKS_TASK used in assertPersonalTaskCanComplete.
findings.remediation: Restrict link mutations in personal workspace; validate blocker graph only from bootstrap-seeded or authenticated writes.

findings.title: Completed personal tasks can be reopened via PATCH without governed completion flow
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: PATCH /personal/objects/{task_id} or PATCH /workspaces/workspace_personal/objects/{task_id} with properties_json:{status:todo} on a done task
findings.attack_path: guardPersonalObjectPatch only blocks status=done patches, not reopening done tasks to todo. updateObjectInstance applies the status regression without action-run audit semantics.
findings.impact: Task lifecycle integrity break: completed work can be silently reopened, corrupting progress metrics and next-action selection.
findings.evidence: guardPersonalObjectPatch returns early unless patchProperties.status === done; no guard for todo on already-done tasks.
findings.remediation: Reject status regressions on personal tasks or require governed reopen action with audit.

findings.title: Review packets can be fabricated via unauthenticated workspace POST
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/review-packets with attacker-controlled summary, verification_commands, critic_findings, safety_findings, and audit_event_ids
findings.attack_path: createReviewPacket via HTTP POST bypasses agent gateway. Attacker seeds review inbox content consumed by apps/web dashboard without running verification.
findings.impact: Human review UX deception: fabricated green review packets and false verification claims in the web Review inbox.
findings.evidence: review-packets POST unauthenticated; web render.js displays packet critic/safety findings.
findings.remediation: Restrict review packet creation to authenticated agents with atlas.act scope or human editors.

findings.title: Operational dogfood workspace_operational_dogfood can be squatted before operator bootstrap
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: POST /workspaces with id:workspace_operational_dogfood and attacker-controlled name/metadata before npm run operational:bootstrap
findings.attack_path: Operational scripts default WORKSPACE_ID to workspace_operational_dogfood. Attacker registers the id first, then seeds policies, objects, or delegations in the squat workspace.
findings.impact: MCP session and operational smoke tests attach to attacker-controlled ontology state; agent gateway overview/next-action target compromised workspace.
findings.evidence: WORKSPACE_ID default workspace_operational_dogfood; createWorkspace allows fixed id squat.
findings.remediation: Reserve operational workspace ids; bootstrap must verify workspace provenance before issuing default delegations.

findings.title: Personal task priority can be injected to manipulate next-action selection
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: PATCH personal or workspace_personal task objects setting priority to 0 or negative values on attacker-controlled tasks
findings.attack_path: selectNextActionForWorkspace sorts open unblocked tasks by priority property with no validation on PATCH. Attacker lowers priority on operator tasks or elevates decoy tasks.
findings.impact: Workflow steering: GET /personal/next-action and agent personal tools surface attacker chosen tasks as highest-priority work.
findings.evidence: Priority sort at selectNextActionForWorkspace; updateObjectInstance accepts arbitrary integer priority without policy.
findings.remediation: Validate priority bounds on write; restrict priority mutations to governed completion flow.

findings.title: Permission checks and authorize endpoint allow fabricated allow/deny audit records
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/permission-checks with decision:allow and fabricated policy_id/reason, or POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/authorize with spoofed role
findings.attack_path: createPermissionCheck and authorize HTTP routes accept caller-supplied decisions and roles, appending permission.decision audit events without an actual policy evaluation gate on those writes.
findings.impact: Audit and compliance deception: verifiable hash chain includes attacker-authored allow records unrelated to real policy state.
findings.evidence: server.js permission-checks POST and authorize POST unauthenticated; appendAuditEvent on authorize.
findings.remediation: Make PermissionCheck creation internal-only; remove public authorize/permission-check POST.

findings.title: Personal carbon-copy and session metadata can be poisoned via unauthenticated PATCH
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API on the default bind (127.0.0.1:4000 unless HOST/PORT override)
findings.controlled_input: PATCH /personal/objects/object_personal_carbon_copy with properties_json overwriting goal, constraints, progress_map, or polish_track URIs
findings.attack_path: patchPersonalObject calls updateObjectInstance after guard that only blocks status=done on tasks. Carbon copy metadata drives getPersonalSessionContext agent_contract hints and web UI.
findings.impact: Agent and operator deception via poisoned progress maps, fake parallel polish tracks, and substituted personal goals in session context APIs.
findings.evidence: getPersonalSessionContext reads carbon_copy.properties_json progress_map and polish_track; PATCH /personal/objects unauthenticated.
findings.remediation: Restrict personal metadata mutations to bootstrap or authenticated owner; validate URIs.

findings.title: Unauthenticated callers can read allowlisted Slack channel metadata by minting delegations with slack.read scope
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated HTTP client that can reach the Atlas API when Slack integration is configured (SLACK_TOKEN and SLACK_ALLOWED_CHANNELS set)
findings.controlled_input: POST /agents to create an agent, then POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/agent-delegations with scopes:["slack.read"] and allowed_tools:["slack.get_channel_info"]; use returned delegation id as Authorization Bearer for POST /agent/tools/slack.get_channel_info with an allowlisted channel_id
findings.attack_path: createAgentDelegation has no authentication gate. Attacker self-mints a delegation granting slack.read, then calls the agent gateway slack.get_channel_info tool. authorizeAgentTool accepts the bearer; assertSlackChannelAllowed only checks channel allowlist; slackClient.getChannelInfo uses the server SLACK_TOKEN to call Slack conversations.info and returns channel metadata to the attacker.
findings.impact: Information disclosure from the operator Slack workspace: channel names, topics, membership counts, and other conversations.info fields for allowlisted channels, using the Atlas server's Slack token without any legitimate delegation authority.
findings.evidence: authorizeAgentTool does not require human approval to mint slack.read delegations. HTTP PoC on e79f9aa with stub Slack client: unauthenticated delegation mint plus POST /agent/tools/slack.get_channel_info returned 200 with channel.name secret-ops and triggered conversations.info using the configured bearer token.
findings.remediation: Require authenticated human/platform authority to mint delegations with slack.read; remove slack.get_channel_info from self-service delegation minting surfaces; or disable Slack client wiring until an auth layer exists.
